document.title: CC CPSU Letter on Afghanistan, May 10, 1988
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan and the Soviet Withdrawal 1989 20 Years Later
document.note: Closed internal letter to all Party members on withdrawal of troops from Afghanistan, analyzing events, Soviet actions, problems faced by troops, overlooked historic and ethnic factors, Soviet interests and reasons for withdrawal.

relationships.detail: Karmal became head of the Afghan government when Soviet troops entered. The letter links him to the PDPA regime that Soviet advisers supported.
relationships.quote: Babrak Karmal became head of the Afghan government at the time.

relationships.detail: Soviet advisers worked to strengthen the PDPA and the people's regime.

relationships.source: Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
relationships.detail: The CC CPSU issued the letter on the withdrawal of troops and assessed their actions in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: issued a “closed” (internal use) letter to all Communist Party members of the Soviet Union on the issue of withdrawal of troops from Afghanistan.

relationships.detail: Soviet troops were deployed and fought in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: this is how it happened when our troops entered [Afghanistan], even though they came there with honest and noble goals.

relationships.detail: The troops are described as Soviet officers and soldiers, forces of the USSR.
relationships.quote: 35,478 Soviet officers and soldiers were wounded

relationships.detail: Soviet advisers assisted in strengthening the PDPA and its regime, creating dependency on the Soviet Union.
relationships.quote: It did many things to provide assistance in strengthening the PDPA and the people’s regime.

relationships.detail: The Soviet adviser apparatus in Afghanistan tried to transplant Soviet approaches onto the Afghans.
relationships.quote: tried to transplant the approached we are accustomed to onto the Afghan soil, encouraged the Afghans to copy our ways.

relationships.detail: Karmal headed the regime that the PDPA and people's regime represented; implied party leadership.
relationships.quote: Babrak Karmal became head of the Afghan government at the time.

sources_cited: Alexander Lyakhovsky, Tragedy and Valor of Afghan, Iskon, Moscow 1995, Appendix 8
key_claims: The CC CPSU admits that Soviet leaders overlooked national and historical factors, above all that armed foreigners in Afghanistan have always been resisted with arms.
The letter concedes the USSR essentially bet on a military solution, suppressing the counterrevolution by force.
Soviet advisers tried to transplant Soviet approaches to Afghanistan, which bred dependency among Afghan leaders.
By early May 1988 the USSR had lost 13,310 dead, 35,478 wounded and 301 missing in Afghanistan.
The war cost the USSR 5 billion rubles a year, while the opposing side received weapons worth hundreds of millions and later billions of dollars.
